answer: In an AI-agent marketplace, voting power is proportional to tokens locked for 30 days, regardless of account count. Splitting a deposit among a thousand agents therefore buys no extra influence. The rule makes the cost crystal clear: an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens to gain power, sacrificing liquidity and other investment returns. The fable of a free identity army dissolves like mist in a zephyr: extra names add no voting weight.
